title: Omit delivery metadata from MCP result; keep only drill-down ids
context: MCP clients show the model exactly one channel (structuredContent or content, not both). Hunch was exposing rank, delivery_reason, provenance_status, and token_cost for every delivered record, redundant metadata the model never sees and the host already holds in receipts. Touches invariant(s): con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: compactEnvelope() reduces delivered/supplements entries to {kind, record_id} only — enough to drill-down via hunch_why(), nothing more. Rank, costs, and provenance stay in the served receipt and the delivery ledger. Same footprint optimization applies to omitted samples: detail sentences dropped, replaced with reason+ids only.
consequences: MCP result payload shrinks; smaller context overhead for the model
Single source of truth: metadata (rank, costs, provenance) lives in receipts, not duplicated in the result
Cost accounting now correct: hunch_context footprint is max(content_chars, structured_chars), not sum (host pays for one channel)
Drill-down remains available (hunch_why) but requires an explicit call, matching the model's actual access pattern
alternatives_rejected: Keep full metadata in MCP result: wasteful duplication, increases footprint, model doesn't use these fields
Include both channels in footprint calculation: misrepresents actual cost (host pays for one, not both)
Sum both channels even though only one is visible: inflates perceived hunch_context footprint
